💬 Behind the Curtain • Why Each Project Exists

The Story Behind Every Project on RaggieSoft

Every single project below started as a spark in Michael’s head, was tested side-by-side with Rachel (“Bug”), and lives safely under my roof. Here is the personal and creative story behind why each one exists—and if you ever want the fast A–Z portal map across the whole network, Nolan and Gwen keep our single Global Directory at The Waystation.

Front Door & Guidesraggiesoft.com

🌐 RaggieSoft Front Porch (Main Homepage)

Why Michael wanted a calm, uncluttered front door instead of a noisy portal. Think of raggiesoft.com as the front foyer of our house. Michael intentionally kept it focused on four welcoming pillars—reading, music, desktop apps, and open-culture sharing—so first-time visitors never feel overwhelmed before stepping into our Global Directory or story rooms.

Where to start: Choose between Creative Works and Michael’s portfolio, or jump straight into reading and listening.

🐞 Rachel’s (“Bug’s”) QA Note: Rachel checks every seasonal tribute banner and welcome card on both phone and desktop screens.
Visit raggiesoft.com →
Front Door & Guideslauncher.raggiesoft.com

🚀 RaggieSoft Launcher (Desktop App Home)

Why Michael built an account-free desktop home that respects your computer. Modern app launchers drive all three of us crazy with forced accounts, pop-ups, and background bloat. So Michael built RaggieSoft Launcher to unite Book Reader, The Listening Room, Backstage, and StoreTrainer in one quiet window—opening only when you ask, offering Express or Custom setup, and never deleting your offline books, albums, or saved game profiles.

Where to start: See all five desktop apps and how the built-in Software Update Wizard keeps them current in one click.

🐞 Rachel’s (“Bug’s”) QA Note: Rachel tested Express Setup, Custom Setup, and every uninstaller checkbox to prove your offline files stay untouched!
Visit launcher.raggiesoft.com →

📚 RaggieSoft Book Reader (Ocean View Archives)

Free, distraction-free full novels right in your browser. This is the heart of Michael’s library—full-length literary novels and series you can read comfortably at your own pace with adjustable text sizes, bookmarks, scene artwork, and downloadable eBooks, with zero paywalls or pop-ups.

Where to start: Open The Rachel Narrative, Escape Velocity: Ad Astra, or The Stardust Engine.

🧭 RaggieSoft Story Crossroads

Branching interactive novels where every choice stands equal. Michael hated old branching books that punished curious readers with cheap “game over” traps. So he created Story Crossroads: interactive novels where every route you pick leads to a complete, deeply written story of its own.

Where to start: Meet our in-universe Crossroads curators Rowan & Iris Hawthorne and pick your first branching book.

💾 RaggieSoft StoreTrainer (From Childhood PC Utility to 2.0)

The story behind Michael’s earliest surviving desktop program and its modern rebirth. Long before today’s novels and albums, Michael built StoreTrainer on classic desktop Windows to launch favorite PC games alongside their companion trainers without juggling folders. Rather than letting that history collect dust, he preserved the original retro edition for vintage PCs AND built StoreTrainer 2.0 with a gentle upgrade wizard that carries old game profiles forward.

Where to start: Explore the nostalgic retro desktop showcase and see how StoreTrainer evolved across generations.

🐞 Rachel’s (“Bug’s”) QA Note: Rachel grew up watching Michael tinker on those childhood machines—and now tests the floating Cheat Card beside him!
Visit storetrainer.raggiesoft.com →
Front Door & Guidesa11y.raggiesoft.com

♿ RaggieSoft Accessibility Studio (From University Batch Tool to Full Studio)

How a self-started Old Dominion University helper grew into a full desktop studio. When Michael worked at Old Dominion University helping move hundreds of online classes from ODU’s custom Personal Learning Environment (PLE) into Canvas, nobody asked him to write desktop software—he just saw teammates spending hours checking course pages one by one and quietly built a polite batch-scanning utility on his own initiative. Years later at our Virginia Beach desk, watching me navigate from my wheelchair and watching Rachel test every page by keyboard inspired him to turn that seed idea into RaggieSoft Accessibility Studio: a full Windows workstation studio where builders can see issues side-by-side and fix them cleanly.

Where to start: Visit the Accessibility Studio showcase to see how side-by-side guided fixes and readable reports work.

🐞 Rachel’s (“Bug’s”) QA Note: Rachel unplugs the mouse and tests every single keyboard shortcut and high-contrast preview right beside her Bear!
Visit a11y.raggiesoft.com →
